what_its_for: Pentamidine is used to prevent or treat a serious lung infection called Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP). This type of infection most often affects people with weakened immune systems, such as those with HIV/AIDS. The inhaled form (breathing treatment) is usually used to prevent PCP, while the injection form is used to treat an active infection.
how_to_take: This medicine comes in two forms. The INHALED form is breathed in through a special nebulizer (breathing machine) — never swallow it or inject it. Breathe slowly and deeply through your mouth during the treatment. The INJECTION form is given by a nurse or doctor into a vein (IV) or muscle over at least 60 minutes — never rush the injection. Always follow the exact instructions from your healthcare team for whichever form you are using.
dosing: For PREVENTION (inhaled): The usual dose is 300 mg breathed in through the nebulizer once every 4 weeks. For TREATMENT (injection): The usual dose is 4 mg per kilogram of body weight given once daily for 14 to 21 days. Your doctor will decide the right dose and length of treatment for you. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of the inhaled form, contact your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to reschedule your breathing treatment — do not just skip it. For the injection form given in a hospital or clinic, your healthcare team will manage your schedule. Never try to 'catch up' by doubling your dose.
storage: Store the dry powder (before mixing) at room temperature, away from light and heat. Keep it out of the reach of children. Once the powder is mixed into a liquid solution, use it right away or store it in the refrigerator and use within 24 to 48 hours. Do not freeze the mixed solution. Dispose of any unused solution as directed by your pharmacist or healthcare provider.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking cigarettes, as this can irritate your lungs, especially during inhaled treatments. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase the risk of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Avoid skipping doses, as this can allow the infection to return or worsen. If you are pregnant or trying to become pregnant, talk to your doctor before using this medicine. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or lightheaded after your treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden chest pain or tightness, severe shortness of breath or wheezing, fast or irregular heartbeat, signs of low blood sugar such as shakiness, sweating, confusion, or fainting, signs of high blood sugar such as extreme thirst, frequent urination, or blurry vision, severe nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), unusual bruising or bleeding, rash or allergic reaction, or numbness or tingling in your hands or feet.
when_it_works: For PREVENTION: Pentamidine helps protect your lungs from getting a PCP infection when you take it regularly every 4 weeks. For TREATMENT: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting the injections, but it usually takes the full 14 to 21 days of treatment to fully fight the infection. Always complete the full course of treatment even if you feel better.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: This medicine may harm an unborn baby. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. KIDNEY OR LIVER DISEASE: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely if you have kidney or liver problems. OLDER ADULTS: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as low blood pressure and kidney problems and will need careful monitoring. CHILDREN: Pentamidine can be used in children, but the dose will be carefully calculated by the doctor based on the child's weight.
